questions.subject: ENGLISH_LITERATURE
questions.topic: Mrs Dalloway and its two narrative threads
questions.learningObjective: Explain how the two narrative threads of the novel are arranged
questions.stem: A signal box noticeboard explains the shape of a single day in a novel whose two stories are set hours apart.

answer.exemplar: The novel runs two threads through the same London day: a hostess moving through the morning towards an evening party, and a shell-shocked veteran whose story reaches the reader through the people who try to help him. The threads are not alternatives to each other; the second exists to test what the first celebrates, and the reader learns of the veteran's death only through the first thread's social machinery.

questions.explanation: The two threads share the city and the day, and the second reaches us through the professionals who link it to the first. Their meeting turns a party narrative into a test of the party.
questions.hint: Ask how the second thread reaches the reader.

questions.learningObjective: Explain why the novel devotes a whole volume to one ordinary day
questions.stem: A line supervisor's note describes a novel that fills a whole day without moving its plot much.

answer.exemplar: The novel treats an ordinary day as an event worth an entire volume, and it does so by extending the smallest sensations until they fill the reader's mind with the same completeness as a plot. The day has no festival and no crisis attached to it, so the reader's attention is redirected to what passes unnoticed in a life, and the book's method becomes its argument about where meaning is actually located.

questions.explanation: The novel extends ordinary moments rather than advancing a plot, so attention moves from events to experience. The day carries no public occasion, which lets the method become the argument.

options.text: The second was shorter, which is why its author finished it ahead of schedule.

options.text: One filled a magazine's pages on demand while the other was built to build a readership.

questions.explanation: One serial was written to fill pages a magazine needed, and the haste shows in its sprawling structure; the other was planned as a run of parts to build a readership. Same format, different logic.

Because the author was a doctor who wanted to show his medical knowledge.

questions.topic: The Little Review prosecution and what it decided
questions.learningObjective: Explain what the campaign against the serial left behind in the law
questions.stem: A token exchange note asks what the campaign against a serialised novel left behind in the law.

options.text: A new rule requiring all fiction to be reviewed before publication.
options.misconception: believes the campaign produced a new statutory rule

options.text: No change to the law; only the injunction against that one work was lifted.
A permanent ban on the review that had published the instalments.
options.misconception: supposes the review itself was permanently banned

options.text: A ruling that every novel must carry a note about its own content.
options.misconception: invents a ruling that novels must carry content notes

questions.explanation: The campaign produced no change in the law; it produced a decision about one book, and the ban on that book was lifted. The machinery the campaign had used stayed available for the next complaint.
questions.hint: Ask what changed and what did not.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LITERATURE
questions.topic: Mrs Dalloway and its two narrative threads
questions.learningObjective: Explain what joining the two earlier pieces of writing achieved
questions.stem: The halt platform card describes a novel that grew out of two earlier pieces of writing and asks what joining them achieved.

answer.exemplar: The novel began as two separate stories, one about a hostess getting through a day in London and one about a shell-shocked man in a hospital, and their combination turned two exercises in consciousness into a single argument. Because the threads run in parallel and are joined only by a professional link, the reader is made to hold two kinds of awareness at once, and the party at the end of the day becomes a test of what the second thread has shown.

questions.explanation: Joining the two pieces made two separate exercises in consciousness into one comparative argument about what people can endure. The parallel structure lets each thread judge the other without meeting.
questions.hint: Ask what two separate stories became when combined.

questions.learningObjective: Identify how the final section differs in voice from the three before it
questions.stem: A station noticeboard asks how a novel's last section differs in voice from the three before it.

options.text: It is written in the plural, giving the family a collective voice it never had.
options.misconception: thinks the last section gives the family a collective voice

options.text: It returns to the first person, picking up the voice of the opening section.
options.misconception: expects the ending to return to the opening's first person

options.text: It steps outside every character and reports the family's fate directly.
It is written as a letter, addressed to a reader the book had not addressed before.
options.misconception: believes the ending addresses the reader directly

questions.explanation: The last section withdraws to a narrator outside the family, who can report deaths and outcomes the characters could only hint at. The change of voice states the book's verdict.
questions.hint: Ask whose voice the final section is not.
